solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bar in joint shortly receiving musical backing

indicators.note: 'shortly' means in short form, so ELBOW is cut short by its last letter
backing means moving backwards, so the finished ELCATSBO is read in reverse

blocks.note: ELBOW, a joint, minus its last letter
the Lloyd Webber show, placed inside ELBO to make ELCATSBO

explanation.surface: A bar where a spliff is passed round while music plays in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks as if it only turns CATS round, but it reverses the whole ELCATSBO; 'joint' is a body part, not a pub or a spliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar across a road is a barrier, and an obstacle is the same thing in general terms.

clue.text: Lazy bishop with single mention of God’s image

indicators.note: to mention a word is to say it, so we want the sound of 'idol'

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation
single = one
an idol is the image of a god

explanation.surface: A bishop who can't be bothered, giving God only one passing mention in his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lazy bishop' reads as one phrase, but the bishop is only B.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the British intensified form, idle right through to the bone.

clue.text: Lesson that’s annoying, with two interpretations of Oman’s capital

indicators.note: the phrase after it must be read in two different ways, each yielding letters

blocks.note: the click of the tongue you make when something annoys you
first reading: capital letter of Oman
second reading: capital as money; the rial is Oman's currency

explanation.surface: A pupil sighs through a geography lesson on the capital of Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue announces it will use 'Oman's capital' twice: once as its first letter, once as its money. The real capital, Muscat, is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a teaching session, usually one tutor with a few students.

clue.text: Raccoon-like mammal’s trimmed fur

indicators.note: trimming cuts a little off the end, so COATI loses its final I

blocks.note: COATI, a South American relative of the raccoon, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A furrier describes a pelt from a raccoon-like animal, clipped short.
explanation.walkthrough: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative from the Americas; one letter off it and its fur appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the natural hairy covering of an animal.

clue.text: Heavenly city opening for atheist in error

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the A of atheist
'in' places that A inside the word for error

blocks.note: the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite
a sin is a moral error
first letter of atheist, placed inside SIN to make SIAN

explanation.surface: An atheist wrongly setting out to find the city of heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly city' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Heavenly'; ELY is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the Greek paradise of the blessed, so its adjective means of paradise.

clue.text: American in Virgin spacecraft

blocks.note: the Virgin Mary
a craft that touches down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: An American riding on one of Richard Branson's Virgin spaceships.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin reads as the Branson company; it is the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone from the state of Maryland is one kind of US citizen.

clue.text: Harmonious arrangement ruined if he sung

indicators.note: something ruined is broken up, so IF HE SUNG is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A lovely musical arrangement that a poor singer would spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about singing and harmony, so 'arrangement' sounds musical; it is the arrangement of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese art of placing rooms and objects so that energy flows in balance.

clue.text: Getting into a lather largely due to obsession

indicators.note: 'largely' means for the most part

blocks.note: as in 'died from', due to
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: Someone working themselves into a state over their obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting into a lather' is both the literal foaming and the idiom for getting worked up, which is what the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally producing suds or foam, and also the idiom for becoming agitated.

clue.text: Player struggling to control each extended period

indicators.note: struggling means thrashing about, so the letters of PLAYER are thrown out of order
to control is to hold in one's grip

blocks.note: anagram of PLAYER
EA is the standard abbreviation for each, placed after the L

explanation.surface: A sportsman battling to stay on top through every long spell of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' is the natural definition for a surface about sport, but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year gains 29 February, so it is a stretch of time lengthened by a day.

clue.text: A French girlfriend, potentially volatile

blocks.note: un = a, the French indefinite article
a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend; 'potentially' says a girlfriend is only one kind

explanation.surface: A man warned that his French girlfriend has a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: a girlfriend is one kind of steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something liable to shift or give way suddenly.

clue.text: Losing focus, Ctrl perhaps opens small window up?

indicators.note: the focus is the centre, so losing it removes KEY's middle letter
to open something is to stand at its start

blocks.note: slight = small
Ctrl is a key on a keyboard; KEY without its middle letter

explanation.surface: A computer user whose eyes glaze over, hitting Ctrl so a tiny window pops up on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all computing, so 'window' is a pop-up box; it is a real window in a roof, and the question mark admits the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof window facing the heavens, so a window placed up high.

clue.text: Join investment scheme with carrier bag, lacking good capital

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it

blocks.note: to add is to join on
an ISA is a British tax-free savings account
British Airways, an air carrier
the word itself
G = good, removed from BAG to leave BA

explanation.surface: Advice to sign up to a savings plan and take a carrier bag, though not a nice one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in a sentence about investment; it is a capital city. 'Carrier bag' reads as one thing but splits into an airline and a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ethiopia's seat of government.

clue.text: Hand position — is it raised first?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards

blocks.note: the word itself
it = sex appeal, SA
a stance is a position, physical or in argument

explanation.surface: A pupil asking whether the hand goes up before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention. 'Hand' is not a raised hand but help, as in 'give me a hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to lend a hand means to help, so a hand is help given.

clue.text: About to mingle with welcome drink

indicators.note: mingling is mixing together

blocks.note: CA = circa, about
hi is a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A host about to circulate among guests with a welcome drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'About' is CA on its own, and 'to mingle' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: spiced Indian milky tea.

clue.text: Nasty male will want to discard wife

indicators.note: discarding is throwing away

blocks.note: HE'LL = he will
to want = to wish
W = wife, removed from WISH to leave ISH

explanation.surface: A cruel man planning to leave his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male will' reads as a man's testament or resolve, but it is the contraction HE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: infernal, extremely unpleasant.

clue.text: On reflection, some reworded a memo, hardly unmanufactured

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters read backwards
'some' asks for only part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run through rework(ED A MEMO H)ardly

explanation.surface: An office worker who rewrote a memo but barely changed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' looks like part of the definition, 'hardly unmanufactured', but it only lends its H to the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Made at home by hand rather than in a factory, so not a manufactured product.

clue.text: Something for chaps, cheek by jowl, finally entering bar

indicators.note: 'finally' points to the final letter of jowl

blocks.note: lip and cheek both mean insolence
bar = save, as in 'all bar one'
last letter of jowl, placed inside SAVE

explanation.surface: A men's grooming product for the face, cheek by jowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaps' reads as men, but it is chapped lips. 'Cheek by jowl' is a phrase meaning side by side, broken up here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on chaps: a soothing balm for chapped lips.

clue.text: Signal for E in between eg newspaper work

indicators.note: 'between' asks for the pieces to sit between the two letters of EG

blocks.note: in Morse code E is a single dot, spoken as 'dit'
the word itself
the word itself, opened to take DIT IN

explanation.surface: A newspaper instruction about an E symbol placed between examples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the container word, but it is a piece of the answer; the container is 'between'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: preparing copy for print is the core job on a newspaper.

clue.text: Setter supporting what 6 might find flat and very boring

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means holding up from below

blocks.note: 6 is MARYLANDER, an American, who spells tyre TIRE
so = very
the setter is 'me'

explanation.surface: A setter's cross-reference that a solver finds dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 6 supplies 'American', so the tyre takes the US spelling TIRE. 'Very boring' looks like the definition, but 'very' is SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dull and wearying.

clue.text: Extremely large naan to tear, freshly produced?

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so large gives L and E
to tear is to rip apart, so the letters are pulled apart and rearranged

blocks.note: first and last letters of large
anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A huge naan bread ripped apart straight from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly produced' sounds like hot bread; it means newborn, and the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to newborn babies, who are freshly produced; the question mark flags the jokey phrasing.

clue.text: I put up with left-wing liberal taking university over

indicators.note: turned over, as in flipped

blocks.note: red = left-wing
Lib = Liberal
U = university, inside LIB to make LIUB

explanation.surface: Someone who has tolerated a left-wing liberal taking over the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I put up with' reads as 'I tolerated'; the definition stops at 'I put up', spoken by the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer speaks: this tradesman is someone who puts up houses and walls.

clue.text: Cleaner energy pessimist

blocks.note: a mop cleans floors
E = energy

explanation.surface: A gloomy doubter of green power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner energy' reads as renewable power, but splits into a MOP and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: someone gloomy and listless who expects the worst.

clue.text: Old-fashioned cricketer’s 2 for 4?

blocks.note: square = conventional, old-fashioned
Joe Root, the England batsman

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: a fusty old player taking two wickets for four runs.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 for 4' is cricket shorthand for two wickets for four runs, which the surface wants; it is maths instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics: 2 multiplied by itself makes 4, so 2 stands in that relation to 4.

clue.text: Part of dish to be arranged by length during dinner?

blocks.note: TBA is the standard abbreviation for to be arranged
L = length, placed after TBA
a meal, opened after its A to take TBA L

explanation.surface: A caterer's note that part of the dinner menu is still undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be arranged' looks like an anagram instruction; it is the abbreviation TBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one ball of minced meat among several in a dish.

clue.text: Pint and three quarters of liquid diesel in the van

indicators.note: the van is the front of an army, so we want the first letter

blocks.note: milk, a liquid; three quarters of it is MIL
first letter of diesel

explanation.surface: A pint of fuel and a tank three quarters full of diesel in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a dark, low-strength British beer ordered by the pint. 'Van' is the vehicle in the surface; here it means the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A British bar order: asking for a pint means a glass of this dark, low-strength beer.

clue.text: One on one contest led by host nation

indicators.note: to be led is to follow a leader

blocks.note: a DJ hosts a radio show
I = one
a bout is a contest, as in boxing
the second one, I

explanation.surface: A one-on-one match headed by the country staging the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host nation' reads as a single phrase for the organiser; 'host' is the DJ and 'nation' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the small republic in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Perhaps Man United no longer deployed video recorder when out of formation

indicators.note: deployed means spread out into position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: 13 letters to start
an order is a formation, as in battle order; removed, leaving VIDEOREC to rearrange

explanation.surface: Manchester United no longer lining up in formation with a video recorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man United' is not the football club but a man who is no longer married, and 'Perhaps' says a woman would do as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose marriage has ended is no longer joined to his wife; 'Perhaps' marks him as one example.

clue.text: Sincerely accepting award for a fish

indicators.note: 'for' means in place of, so the award replaces the letter A

blocks.note: sincerely = really, truly
Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour; it takes the place of REALLY's A

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely accepting an award on behalf of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fish' reads as the definition, but 'for a' is the swap instruction and 'fish' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a name for several fish with red undersides, such as the char.
